This article highlights seven virtual reality stocks to consider, including the ProShares Metaverse ETF (VERS) for diversification, Roblox (RBLX) as a leading social metaverse platform, and tech giants like Microsoft (MSFT) and Apple (AAPL) that are heavily investing in VR/AR. Other recommendations include Nvidia (NVDA) for its Omniverse platform, Matterport (MTTR) for its exposure to "digital twins," and Unity Software (U) which recently received a "buy" rating.

title: Oracle Cloud adds NVIDIA chips, software to speed enterprise AI uptake
summary: Oracle has expanded its partnership with NVIDIA to integrate tens of thousands of NVIDIA's AI-processing graphics chips and software tools into Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). This aims to accelerate enterprise AI adoption across industries like banking, healthcare, and manufacturing by offering powerful A100 and upcoming H100 GPUs. The collaboration will also provide access to NVIDIA software like RAPIDS Accelerator and Clara for enhanced AI performance, medical imaging, and drug discovery.

title: Oracle and NVIDIA Partner to Speed AI Adoption for Enterprises
summary: Oracle and NVIDIA have expanded their long-standing alliance through a multi-year partnership aimed at accelerating AI adoption for enterprises. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) will significantly increase its GPU capacity with NVIDIA's A100 and upcoming H100 GPUs, supporting the full stack of NVIDIA AI software and services. This collaboration will provide enterprises with a broad, accessible portfolio for AI training and deep learning inference, integrating NVIDIA AI platforms into OCI to drive innovation across various industries.

title: Adobe Advances 3D, Immersive and Metaverse Experiences With New Products
summary: Adobe announced significant advancements in its Substance 3D tools, introducing new products like 3D Capture and Substance 3D Modeler to facilitate the creation of 3D and metaverse-ready immersive experiences. The company also revealed a partnership with Meta to integrate Substance 3D tools into the Quest platform, making 3D content creation more accessible. These innovations aim to support creators and brands in transitioning into new mediums, emphasizing ease of use and sustainability with a new Substance 3D Sustainability Calculator.

title: Supermicro Extends Best of Breed Server Building Block Solutions to Include a Broad Set of OCP Technologies - Driving Customer Innovation and Time-to-Market
summary: Supermicro is expanding its server portfolio to incorporate open hardware and open-source technologies, aiming to drive innovation and reduce proprietary lock-in for customers. These solutions, including an 8U 8-GPU AI training system and OCP 3.0 compliant AIOM cards, integrate best-in-class components like Intel, AMD, and ARM CPUs and NVIDIA GPUs, alongside open technologies such as OpenBMC and Open BIOS. This initiative provides customers with high-performance, efficient, and flexible server options for various applications, from cloud and AI/ML to storage and 5G/Edge computing.

title: Samsung, Qualcomm unveil industry’s fastest LPDDR5X DRAM chip
summary: Samsung Electronics Co. has successfully demonstrated the performance of its LPDDR5X DRAM on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon mobile platform, achieving an industry-leading speed of 8.5 gigabits per second (Gbps). This advancement surpasses Samsung's previous record and solidifies its leadership in the memory market. The new high-speed, low-power memory is expected to enhance mobile, gaming, camera, and AI applications and find broader use in PCs, HPC, servers, and autonomous driving.

title: Gartner Top 10 Tech Trends For 2023: Metaverse, AI, Cloud
summary: Gartner has released its top 10 technology trends for 2023, focusing on themes like optimizing resilience, scaling solutions, and pioneering new opportunities amidst economic uncertainty. The trends include the metaverse, super apps, adaptive AI, industry cloud platforms, and sustainability, emphasizing technology's role in addressing global challenges and driving business value beyond just cost savings. Each trend is accompanied by an example of its real-world application.

title: Credo Announces 1.6Tbps OSFP-XD HiWire AECs Targeting Hyperscaler Spine Switching
summary: Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd announced its new 1.6Tb OSFP-XD HiWire CLOS Active Electrical Cable (AEC), designed for hyperscale data centers requiring high-density spine switching. This AEC supports speeds up to 1.6Tbps, cable lengths up to 2.75m, and consumes less than 20W of power, making it energy-efficient and suitable for next-generation 51.2Tbps switches in a 1U form factor. The product leverages a 12nm process for cost-effectiveness and is being showcased at the OCP Summit.

title: Nvidia closes Russian offices, will fly relocating employees out of the country, report says
summary: Nvidia is ceasing all activities and closing its offices in Russia, offering its employees the opportunity to relocate out of the country. The company had previously suspended shipments to Russia but maintained an office to support employees and their families. Nvidia stated that recent developments have made it impossible to operate effectively there.

title: As NVIDIA Corporation's (NASDAQ:NVDA)) market cap dropped by US$9.4b, insiders who sold US$156m worth of stock were able to offset their losses
summary: Insiders at NVIDIA Corporation sold US$156 million worth of stock over the last year at an average price of US$212 per share, effectively offsetting some losses as the company's market cap dropped by US$9.4 billion. While insider selling occurred, the notable sale by Independent Director Mark Stevens was at a price well above the current stock price, making strong conclusions difficult. Insiders collectively own about 4.0% of the company, valued at US$12 billion, which is seen as a positive sign of alignment with shareholders despite a lack of recent insider buying.

title: Meet the Harvard Law School graduate helping China cut its reliance on US AI chips
summary: Michael Zhang Wen, a Harvard Law School graduate and chairman of Biren Technology, is leading China's efforts to reduce its dependence on US artificial intelligence (AI) chips. His Shanghai-based start-up recently released the BR100, a 7-nanometre GPU, which some believe could position Biren to become "China's Nvidia" amidst escalating US export restrictions on advanced chips. Zhang faces pressure to deliver, as his company has raised a substantial US$655 million from major venture capital funds.

title: TSMC starts mass-producing three-nanometer chips
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (TSMC) has begun mass-producing processors using its advanced three-nanometer chip technology. This new technology offers a 15% improvement in chip performance and up to 35% less power consumption compared to its earlier five-nanometer process. TSMC, a major contract chip manufacturer for companies like Apple, AMD, and Nvidia, plans to develop multiple versions of this technology and is building new fabrication plants in Arizona.

title: How the industrial metaverse will transform manufacturing
summary: The industrial metaverse, leveraging virtual and augmented reality, is transforming manufacturing by enhancing training, collaboration, and the use of digital twins. Companies like Lincoln Electric are using VR for faster and more efficient welder training, while automotive manufacturers like Kia and Volvo are using metaverse technologies for remote design collaboration and virtual prototyping, significantly cutting down development time and costs. Despite challenges like high equipment costs and technical difficulties, the industrial metaverse is gaining traction, with its applications expected to expand beyond initial consumer-focused visions.

title: The bright side of the chip glut: Nvidia, AMD and Intel gaming cards are cheap and very available for Christmas
summary: The article highlights that due to a chip glut, gaming cards from Nvidia, AMD, and Intel are now readily available and significantly discounted, making them an affordable option for Christmas shoppers. This marks a significant change from the previous two years when these items were scarce and expensive. The availability addresses past disappointments for gamers hoping for these cards during the holidays.

title: Alibaba Cloud cuts prices by up to 50% for core, storage products
summary: Alibaba Cloud, the cloud computing division of Alibaba Group, announced price cuts of up to 50% on its core products and services to increase its market share in China amidst growing competition. This move, effective Wednesday, includes reductions for services using Arm, Intel-based chips, and Nvidia GPUs. The company also revealed that over 200,000 enterprises have requested beta testing for its AI-powered large language model, Tongyi Qianwen.

title: NVIDIA Enables Trustworthy, Safe, and Secure Large Language Model Conversational Systems
summary: NVIDIA has introduced NeMo Guardrails, an open-source toolkit designed to ensure the safety, security, and trustworthiness of large language model (LLM) conversational systems. This toolkit allows developers to define programmable rules, known as guardrails, that guide user interactions and prevent off-topic discussions, misinformation, toxicity, and malicious code execution. NeMo Guardrails integrates with existing LLMs and toolkits like LangChain, providing a robust framework for building reliable AI applications.

title: Cognitive Computing Brings Human Touch
summary: Cognitive computing, particularly neuromorphic computing, is poised to transform artificial intelligence by enabling systems to "think" like humans, learn from data, and interact naturally. This technology, which uses artificial neurons to mimic the human brain, could power various applications from autonomous vehicles to smart devices with greater efficiency. While companies developing this technology present investment opportunities, the article suggests that adopting companies leveraging it for increased productivity and growth may offer even greater upside, while also highlighting the ethical considerations and risks associated with advanced AI systems.

title: Prime Minister Pashinyan receives the President and CEO of Nvidia company Jensen Huang
summary: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan met with Jensen Huang, President and CEO of Nvidia, a leader in the high-tech sector. The discussion focused on the development of engineering education, the advancement of the high-tech sector, and continued collaboration between the Armenian government and Nvidia. Nvidia had established a scientific research center in Armenia the previous year, with both parties expressing commitment to further development in the country's IT sector.

title: Alibaba's Hong Kong shares slump on SoftBank's stake sale report
summary: Alibaba's Hong Kong-listed shares fell significantly following reports that SoftBank Group Corp is selling almost all of its remaining stake in the Chinese e-commerce giant. This move comes as valuations for China's big tech firms are recovering after a period of heightened regulatory scrutiny and as SoftBank seeks to monetize profitable holdings amidst efforts to shore up cash reserves for its Vision Fund losses. SoftBank has been shifting to a "defensive mode" and had previously booked a substantial gain by cutting its Alibaba stake last year.

title: 2 Under-The-Radar Small Chip Stocks Poised For Big Growth
summary: This article highlights two under-the-radar fabless semiconductor companies, Impinj Inc. (NASDAQ: PI) and Allegro MicroSystems, Inc. (NASDAQ: ALGM), that are showing strong growth potential despite being smaller players in the chip industry. Both companies are experiencing increasing sales and earnings, with analysts expecting continued growth in the coming years. The article details their specific market niches and financial performance, positioning them as attractive opportunities for investors.

title: Qualcomm, Nvidia spar for top spot in AI chip efficiency tests
summary: Qualcomm's AI 100 chips outperformed Nvidia's H100 chips in two out of three power efficiency categories for AI inference tasks, specifically image classification and object detection. Nvidia, however, took the lead in natural language processing performance and power efficiency. This highlights the competitive landscape in the growing market for data center inference chips, where power consumption is a key cost factor.

title: Best-Performing Stocks of Q1 2023
summary: The first quarter of 2023 saw a significant rebound in technology and communication services stocks, with Nvidia, Meta Platforms, and Salesforce among the top performers. This resurgence was driven by factors such as better-than-expected earnings, cost-cutting measures, and growing enthusiasm for artificial intelligence, contrasting sharply with the downturn experienced in 2022. Other sectors like entertainment and media, cryptocurrency, and electric vehicles also saw notable gains.

title: SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) Stock: Breakout Leveraging Tech Stocks Rally?
summary: The SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) ETF has shown a positive resurgence in 2023, largely driven by gains in tech and semiconductor stocks, which comprise a significant portion of its portfolio. Technical analysis suggests a potential bullish breakout for SPY, with indicators pointing to an upcoming rally. Investors are advised to watch support levels and anticipate a rise leveraging the strength of its underlying tech holdings.

title: Synopsys Launches Full-Stack, AI-Driven EDA Suite
summary: Synopsys has introduced Synopsys.ai, a comprehensive AI-driven suite of solutions for the entire chip design process, from architecture to manufacturing. This suite enables engineers to leverage AI at every stage and access tools via the cloud, significantly reducing product development time and improving silicon performance. Leading semiconductor companies, including Renesas, MediaTek, IBM Research, and TSMC, are already utilizing Synopsys.ai to optimize design, verification, testing, and manufacturing, demonstrating the transformative potential of AI in the semiconductor industry.

title: Synopsys.ai Unveiled as Industry's First Full-Stack, AI-Driven EDA Suite for Chipmakers
summary: Synopsys launched Synopsys.ai, an AI-driven EDA suite for chip design, verification, testing, and manufacturing. This suite allows engineers to use AI at every stage of chip development, significantly boosting productivity, silicon quality, and cost reduction. Market leaders like NVIDIA, TSMC, IBM, MediaTek, and Renesas have tested and supported Synopsys' AI strategy, reporting substantial benefits and efficiency improvements.

title: Supermicro Expands GPU Solutions Portfolio with Deskside Liquid-Cooled AI Development Platform, Powered by NVIDIA
summary: Supermicro has launched a new liquid-cooled AI development platform, the SYS-751GE-TNRT-NV1, designed for deskside use. This platform features four NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs and two 4th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable CPUs, providing a powerful, quiet, and energy-efficient solution for AI/HPC workloads. It also includes a three-year subscription to NVIDIA AI Enterprise, simplifying software setup for developers.

title: Liquid Cooled AI Development Platform
summary: Supermicro has launched a new liquid-cooled AI development platform, developed in partnership with NVIDIA, designed for advanced AI developers. This system features four liquid-cooled NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs, offering over 2 Petaflops of AI performance in a quiet, self-contained unit suitable for various environments. It is available with optional NVIDIA AI Enterprise software and can be customized to specific requirements.

title: AB US Low Volatility Equity ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the AB US Low Volatility Equity ETF (LOWV), which was established on March 22, 2023. The ETF focuses on large- and mid-cap US stocks, actively managed to achieve lower volatility than the broader market. Key holdings include major technology companies like Alphabet, Microsoft, Apple, NVIDIA, and Amazon, alongside diversified investments across various sectors.

title: Raja Koduri, Main Driver Of Intel’s GPU Efforts, To Leave Company
summary: Raja Koduri, Intel's chief architect and the main driver behind its discrete GPU efforts, is leaving the company at the end of March to start a new software company focused on generative AI for gaming, media, and entertainment. Koduri had been with Intel for over five years, leading the buildout of its graphics capabilities and serving as chief architect for most of his tenure. His departure comes as Intel announced cuts to its data center GPU roadmap and delays to Falcon Shores.

title: Demo of China’s Answer to ChatGPT Disappoints Investors
summary: Baidu Inc.'s CEO Robin Li unveiled "Ernie Bot," China's answer to ChatGPT, in a recorded video demonstration that disappointed investors, leading to a 6.4% drop in Baidu's shares. The pre-recorded nature of the demo and lack of real-time interaction raised questions about Ernie's capabilities compared to OpenAI's ChatGPT. Despite the initial disappointment, Baidu is considered a frontrunner in China's AI race, planning to integrate Ernie Bot across its services while navigating concerns about US tech restrictions and Chinese regulatory oversight.

title: Deal Roundup: WeRide files for $500m US listing
summary: WeRide, an autonomous driving technology developer, has confidentially filed for a US IPO aiming to raise up to $500M, with several corporate investors poised for an exit. The deal roundup also highlights CNH Industrial's $110M acquisition of Augmenta Agriculture Technologies and Vivasure Medical's €30M series D funding. Additionally, it details a new €50M fund from Rethink Ventures backed by multiple corporates and various other recent funding rounds across different sectors.

title: Ssangyong E&C wins contract for building ASML Korea campus
summary: Ssangyong Engineering & Construction secured a 200-billion-won ($170-million) contract to build a new campus for ASML Holding NV in Hwaseong, South Korea. The campus, with two buildings totaling 74,418 square meters, will house offices and research facilities for ASML, specializing in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment. This project aims to expand ASML's local supply chain and customer support by enabling more parts procurement in Korea and expanding its partner firm base.

title: Rockwell Automation acquires Knowledge Lens
summary: Rockwell Automation has acquired Bengaluru-based enterprise insights provider Knowledge Lens for an undisclosed sum. This acquisition aims to boost Rockwell's capabilities in data utilization, autonomous manufacturing, and continuous optimization for manufacturers worldwide. Knowledge Lens will join Rockwell's digital services business, Kalypso, to accelerate transformational outcomes for its global clientele, aligning with Rockwell's strategy to expand capabilities and explore early-stage investments in India.

title: Microchip Technology, microchip manufacturer with capital of $50 billion, coming to Armenia
summary: American microchip manufacturer Microchip Technology, with a market capital of $50 billion, is expanding its operations into Armenia. This follows a two-year collaborative agreement with Instigate company, which culminated in Microchip Technology acquiring Instigate Semiconductor. The move is part of a larger trend of major tech and energy companies, including NVIDIA, AMD, and Shell, establishing a presence in Armenia, aiming to boost the country's productivity, innovation, and expertise in high-tech fields.

title: HP CEO Lores: Hybrid Work Is ‘Driving Innovation Across Our Portfolio’
summary: HP CEO Enrique Lores stated that hybrid work is a long-term trend fueling innovation across their portfolio, with their hybrid systems business more than doubling year over year. Despite a general economic downturn and weakening corporate demand impacting PC sales, the company maintains its fiscal year outlook and expects to achieve significant cost savings. HP is also expanding its subscription services and investing in areas like AI and professional workstations.

title: BBLU Top Holdings List & Exposure (EA Bridgeway Blue Chip ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure breakdown for the EA Bridgeway Blue Chip ETF (BBLU). title: Applied Materials stock rises on new chip-making system that helps lower costs
summary: Applied Materials Inc. shares rose after the company unveiled a new chip-making system designed to lower manufacturing costs for semiconductors. The system, called Centura Sculpta, promises to save fabs like TSMC and Intel $50 per wafer. This innovation led to a notable outperformance of Applied Materials stock compared to its peers and the broader semiconductor market.

title: The Future of AI Stocks: 7 Companies to Keep Your Eye On
summary: This article identifies seven key AI stocks and ETFs that investors should consider due to artificial intelligence's potential to revolutionize various industries. It highlights companies like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Advanced Micro Devices for their direct involvement in AI technology, along with Innodata and C3.ai for their specific AI solutions. title: This Week in the Metaverse: BlackRock's new ETF, Titanic artifacts as NFTs, and a Snow Crash Sotheby’s auction
summary: BlackRock has launched a new metaverse ETF, allowing investors to engage with companies contributing to virtual platforms, gaming, and AR/VR. In other news, never-before-seen photos of rapper Tupac Shakur are being released as NFTs, while artifacts from the Titanic will also be preserved and sold as NFTs. Additionally, Sotheby's is holding an auction to celebrate 30 years of Neal Stephenson's "Snow Crash," featuring physical and digital items tied to the seminal metaverse novel.

title: Intel Corp. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Shares of Intel Corp. (INTC) increased by 0.55% to $25.61 on Thursday, outperforming the S&P 500 Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which rose 0.53% and 0.33% respectively. This rise ended a four-day losing streak for Intel, although the stock remains significantly below its 52-week high. Despite the overall positive day for Intel, it underperformed some competitors like NVIDIA Corp.

title: As chatbots boom, Nvidia sales outlook beats Wall Street expectations
summary: Nvidia Corp (NVDA.O) surpassed Wall Street's first-quarter revenue expectations, driven by a surge in demand for its chips used in AI services like chatbots. The company announced a new cloud computing service to help businesses develop generative AI, positioning itself to significantly benefit from the growing AI sector despite a broader downturn in the PC market. Analysts project this boom in generative AI could add an additional $14 billion to Nvidia's revenue by 2027.

title: Meet the $10,000 Nvidia chip powering the race for A.I.
summary: The Nvidia A100 chip, costing around $10,000, has become a critical tool in the artificial intelligence industry, powering applications like ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion. Nvidia dominates the market for GPUs used in machine learning, with the A100 serving as a "workhorse" for AI professionals and requiring substantial investment for companies to train and deploy AI models. Despite the high costs and emerging competition, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang asserts that their GPUs offer a much more affordable solution for developing sophisticated AI models compared to traditional CPU-based data centers.

title: Nvidia adds to AI hype with new cloud-based service, stock jumps on forecast
summary: Nvidia's shares surged after the company announced strong fiscal fourth-quarter results and plans to make its AI software available on major cloud platforms like Oracle, Microsoft, and Alphabet. CEO Jensen Huang highlighted the potential of their new browser-based DGX Cloud AI supercomputer service to accelerate adoption of higher-margin data-center software, capitalizing on the booming interest in artificial intelligence. This move is expected to expand the chip maker's revenue streams beyond hardware.

title: Nvidia earnings overshadowed by Microsoft, ChatGPT, OpenAI, 10-year gaming partnership
summary: Nvidia's upcoming earnings report is largely overshadowed by its new 10-year partnership with Microsoft to bring Activision Blizzard and Xbox games to GeForce Now. This partnership also highlights Nvidia's role in powering AI technologies like OpenAI's ChatGPT, especially given Microsoft's recent investment in OpenAI and plans to integrate its AI across services. The focus is now on Nvidia's data-center sales and its contribution from public cloud providers such as Microsoft Azure.

title: Microsoft teams up with Nvidia and Nintendo in 10-year deal to stream Xbox games
summary: Microsoft has secured 10-year agreements with Nvidia and Nintendo to stream Xbox games as part of its strategy to address antitrust concerns regarding its proposed acquisition of Activision Blizzard. This partnership aims to make Xbox and potential Activision titles available on Nvidia's GeForce Now cloud gaming service and Nintendo platforms, covering various devices. The move is intended to placate regulators scrutinizing the $69 billion deal.

title: Microsoft and NVIDIA Announce Expansive New Gaming Deal
summary: Microsoft and NVIDIA have announced a 10-year partnership to bring Xbox PC games, including Activision Blizzard titles like Call of Duty, to NVIDIA's GeForce NOW cloud gaming service. This agreement will allow over 25 million GeForce NOW members to stream these games across various devices and resolves NVIDIA's concerns regarding Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard, leading NVIDIA to support the regulatory approval of the merger. The collaboration aims to expand gaming choices and make popular titles more accessible through cloud streaming.

title: NVIDIA GTC 2023 to Feature Latest Advances in AI Computing Systems, Generative AI, Industrial Metaverse, Robotics; Keynote by Jensen Huang; Talks by OpenAI, DeepMind Founders
summary: NVIDIA announced its GTC 2023 conference, scheduled for March 20-23, will feature a keynote by CEO Jensen Huang focusing on generative AI, the metaverse, large language models, and robotics. The virtual event expects over 250,000 registrants and more than 650 sessions, including talks from leaders like OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis. GTC 2023 will also offer learning opportunities, dedicated sessions for startups, and a financial analyst Q&A session.

summary: This article analyzes the current hype surrounding generative AI, using the iShares Exponential Technologies ETF (XT) as a proxy for innovation. title: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Shares of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) fell by 0.90% to $85.18 on Wednesday, despite a generally positive trading session for the stock market. The decline broke a two-day winning streak for AMD, which closed significantly below its 52-week high. Compared to competitors, AMD's performance was mixed, with NVIDIA Corp. also falling, while Intel Corp. and Applied Materials Inc. saw gains.

title: Equinix uses two-phase cooling on live Metal cloud servers
summary: Equinix has implemented two-phase liquid cooling on live production servers for its Metal infrastructure-as-a-service offering, using ZutaCore technology. This system, which involves a fluid boiling and condensing to remove heat more efficiently, has been running stably for six months in its NY5 data center. The company is testing this on standard hardware to prepare for higher thermal design power (TDP) servers and address potential future industry needs for more efficient cooling solutions, despite current PUE metrics not fully capturing its benefits.

title: The 3 Best Quantum Computing Stocks to Buy for February 2023
summary: This article highlights the three best quantum computing stocks to consider for February 2023: IBM, IonQ, and Nvidia. It discusses how quantum computing is a rapidly growing field with diverse applications and a projected market value of $1.77 billion annually by 2026. title: CEO longevity pays off for JPMorgan Chase’s Jamie Dimon and other chiefs of World’s Most Admired Companies
summary: This article highlights how CEO longevity, exemplified by Jamie Dimon of JPMorgan Chase, contributes to a company's success and reputation, as seen in Fortune's World's Most Admired Companies list. Long-tenured CEOs develop deep pattern recognition, build strong internal cultures, and foster innovation, leading to greater efficiency and financial performance. summary: Sify Technologies Limited (NASDAQ: SIFY) has been recognized as India's first NVIDIA DGX-Ready data center colocation provider, enabling customers to host NVIDIA DGX A100 systems. Enterprises will benefit from AI-powered insights, efficient ROI on AI infrastructure, and scalable AI clusters for private cloud deployments.

title: 2 Chip Stocks to Buy Instead of NVIDIA In 2023
summary: Despite macroeconomic headwinds and regulatory actions impacting the chip industry, technological advancements and government support are poised to drive long-term growth. (NVDA) due to their robust financials and promising market outlook.

title: Right on Track: NVIDIA Open-Source Software Helps Developers Add Guardrails to AI Chatbots
summary: NVIDIA has released NeMo Guardrails, new open-source software designed to help developers ensure generative AI applications, particularly those powered by large language models, remain accurate, appropriate, on-topic, and secure. This software enables the creation of topical, safety, and security guardrails to prevent AI from veering off course, filtering unwanted language, and restricting connections to safe third-party applications. summary: This article from Zacks Investment Ideas spotlights five stocks across three attractive industry groups: Solar Energy, Medical Products, and Enterprise Software. summary: Rebellions Inc., a South Korean AI chip design startup, plans to mass-produce its ATOM AI chips early next year after its ATOM chip outperformed rivals like Qualcomm and Nvidia in MLPerf tests. The CEO, Park Sung-hyun, aims to surpass Qualcomm within a decade, seeking validation from potential clients like Google and Microsoft, with significant investment already secured from various venture capitalists and institutional investors. The company's success is seen as good news for Korea's semiconductor

title: Cadence Launches Cloud AI Tool to Shrink PCB Placement and Routing Times
summary: Cadence Design Systems has introduced its new Allegro X AI technology, a cloud-based tool designed to automate PCB placement and routing. This AI-driven solution, built on the Allegro X Design Platform, aims to significantly reduce design turnaround times by up to ten times, improving productivity, enhancing quality through early feasibility analysis, and replacing traditional rule-of-thumb methods with a physics-based approach. Early customer testing has shown substantial time savings and improved wire lengths in PCB designs.

title: Google says its AI supercomputer is faster, greener than Nvidia A100 chip
summary: Google has released new details about its custom-designed Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) supercomputers, claiming they are faster and more power-efficient than Nvidia's A100 chip systems. The supercomputers, which have been online since 2020, use optical switches to connect over 4,000 TPUs, allowing for efficient training of large AI models like Google's PaLM. Google hinted at future TPU developments that could compete with Nvidia's current H100 chip.

summary: This article identifies seven top robotics stocks for long-term growth, highlighting the rapid expansion of the robotics market and its increasing integration into various industries. It emphasizes that advancements in computing power and AI are making mechatronic devices capable of complex tasks, with projected market growth reaching $214 billion by 2030. The article details companies like UiPath, iRhythm Technologies, Nvidia, iRobot, Intuitive Surgical, ABB, and Teradyne, discussing their unique contributions and market positions within the robotics sector.

title: Micron Could Report Largest Ever Loss in Q2
summary: Micron Technology Inc. (MU) is projected to report its largest-ever loss in the second fiscal quarter of 2023, with an estimated net loss of nearly $1.2 billion and EPS of -$1.06, a significant drop from the prior year. This financial struggle is attributed to weak consumer demand, high inflation, inventory issues, and industry-wide supply constraints. Analysts predict negative gross margins for the first time in 15 years, with an expected inventory write-down in the range of a billion dollars.

title: Beamr teams with NVIDIA to accelerate Beamr technology on NVIDIA GPUs
summary: Beamr Imaging Ltd. announced that its video encoding technology now supports NVIDIA GPU acceleration, achieving up to 10x faster encoding speeds compared to CPUs. This advancement enables real-time optimization for live video streams, reducing storage and bitrate while maintaining high visual quality. Beamr is collaborating with NVIDIA to develop a cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) offering, with a beta launch planned for Q3 2023, aiming to attract new customers with competitive pricing.

title: Fast, sustainable delivery—thanks to your friendly neighborhood robot
summary: Serve Robotics is leading the way in sustainable, autonomous urban delivery with its zero-emission sidewalk robots, aiming to reduce CO2 emissions from last-mile deliveries. The company has completed over 20,000 deliveries and achieved Level 4 autonomy, operating without human supervision in designated areas. Serve Robotics is rapidly scaling its operations, with plans to expand to new cities and leverage its technology to address broader societal challenges like traffic and accidents.

title: Hedge fund exposure to 7 biggest tech stocks at record high, Goldman Sachs says
summary: Hedge funds have reached record exposure to the seven largest tech stocks by market capitalization, according to Goldman Sachs data, driven by strong performance and the artificial intelligence theme. These seven stocks, including Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft, now constitute about 20% of the total net market value held by hedge funds tracked by Goldman Sachs. Despite the concentration risk, investment managers rationalize these allocations due to the significant returns generated by these companies this year.

summary: Nvidia Corporation (NVDA) is a top holding in many tech, AI, and semiconductor ETFs due to its crucial role in manufacturing GPUs that power AI applications. Despite potential challenges like competition and geopolitical factors, Nvidia's innovative technology and market dominance make it a key component for investors seeking exposure to the rapidly growing AI market. ETFs like the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the Strive U.S. Semiconductor ETF (SHOC) have significant allocations to NVDA, reflecting its importance in the sector.

title: AMD debuts two new graphics cards for the consumer market
summary: AMD has introduced two new graphics cards, the Radeon RX 7800 XT and RX 7700 XT, to compete with Nvidia in the consumer chip market. These cards, priced at $499 and $449 respectively, are positioned as more affordable alternatives to high-end GPUs while offering significant performance per dollar. Based on AMD's latest RDNA 3 architecture, they include features like upgraded machine learning accelerators, ray tracing optimization, and FSR 3 technology for improved gaming visuals.

title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2024
summary: NVIDIA reported record revenue of $13.51 billion for the second quarter of fiscal 2024, a 101% increase from a year ago, driven by strong growth in Data Center revenue at $10.32 billion. The company also announced a new $25.00 billion share repurchase authorization and provided a positive outlook for the third quarter, expecting revenue of $16.00 billion. The CEO highlighted the ongoing transition to accelerated computing and generative AI as key drivers for NVIDIA's success.

title: Arm, the Chip Designer, Files for an I.P.O. Expected to Be Among the Largest (Published 2023)
summary: Arm, the chip design company owned by SoftBank, has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Nasdaq exchange, which is anticipated to be one of the largest in recent years. This move follows Nvidia's abandoned bid to acquire Arm for $40 billion 18 months prior. The IPO will provide SoftBank with additional capital for investments, and SoftBank will retain its position as Arm's controlling shareholder.

title: GraniteShares' Single Stock ETFs Will Follow Nvidia, Tesla, AMD
summary: GraniteShares has launched four new single-stock ETFs to capitalize on the trading momentum of Nvidia, Tesla, and Advanced Micro Devices. These new ETFs offer unique leveraged and short exposures, with the GraniteShares 1.5x Short NVDA Daily ETF (NVD) launching just before Nvidia's earnings report. The asset manager plans to roll out almost three dozen more such filings, emphasizing being first to market with these trading-focused products.

summary: This article provides detailed stock price and quote information for the GraniteShares 2x Short NVDA Daily ETF (NVD), an exchange-traded fund designed to deliver inverse daily returns of NVIDIA Corporation's stock. It includes performance metrics, financial data, and relevant news headlines. The ETF aims to replicate -1.5 times the daily percentage change of NVIDIA's common stock through swap agreements.

title: Report: AI startup Hugging Face hoping to raise millions from Salesforce and other investors
summary: AI startup Hugging Face is reportedly seeking to raise $200 million in venture capital, with Salesforce Inc. expected to lead the funding round. This investment would more than double Hugging Face's current $2 billion valuation, bringing it to $4 billion. The funds will support its platform which hosts over 100,000 open-source AI models and offers paid functionalities like AutoTrain and Inference API.

title: Hesai Reports Record Lidar Sales, Revenue
summary: Hesai Technology (NASDAQ: HSAI) reported record-breaking unaudited financial results for Q2 2023, with quarterly revenue reaching RMB440.3 million ($60.7 million), a 108.5% YoY increase. The company shipped 52,106 lidar units, a 946.5% YoY increase, significantly driven by ADAS lidar growth. Hesai also solidified its position as the No. 1 global automotive lidar supplier, secured new design wins with major OEMs, and deepened its collaboration with NVIDIA.

title: Intel’s Terminated $5.4B Tower Acquisition: 5 Big Things To Know
summary: Intel terminated its $5.4 billion acquisition of Tower Semiconductor due to regulatory approval issues, a setback for CEO Pat Gelsinger's IDM 2.0 strategy and Intel Foundry Services. The deal's failure, possibly due to U.S.-China geopolitical tensions, resulted in a $353 million termination fee. Despite this, Intel remains committed to its foundry business, aiming to become the second-largest global external foundry by 2030, though Tower's capacity and customer base would have provided a significant boost.

title: SK Telecom to invest $100M in AI company Anthropic
summary: SK Telecom announced a $100 million investment in U.S. AI company Anthropic to expand its presence in the AI sector and collaborate on developing an AI platform and large language model. This partnership is expected to accelerate the development of the global Telco AI Platform, aligning with SK Telecom's broader strategy to foster an AI ecosystem with international telecommunications companies. Anthropic's chief scientist will lead the development of a new LLM supporting multiple languages, including Korean, English, German, and Japanese.

title: Opinion: Why Nvidia investors are rattled by Supermicro’s AI chip supply constraints
summary: Nvidia investors are concerned by AI chip supply constraints reported by Supermicro, a Silicon Valley computer and server maker. Supermicro's executives stated they need more AI chips from Nvidia, confirming existing supply limitations for Nvidia's popular graphics chips. This suggests that the high demand for AI applications may face hardware availability issues.

title: Micron Launches Memory Expansion Module Portfolio to Accelerate CXL 2.0 Adoption
summary: Micron Technology announced the sample availability of its CZ120 memory expansion modules, designed to accelerate CXL 2.0 adoption. These modules, available in 128 GB and 256 GB capacities, enhance server systems by providing incremental memory capacity and bandwidth, particularly beneficial for AI, SaaS, and HPC workloads. Micron is collaborating with Intel and AMD to validate the CZ120 modules on their CXL-compatible platforms.

title: AMD's stock breaks with chip selloff to finish week higher as analyst cites 'important buying opportunity'
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares unexpectedly rose last week, up 2.6%, despite a broader chip sector selloff that saw Nvidia and the PHLX Semiconductor Index decline significantly. An analyst pointed to this performance as an "important buying opportunity" for AMD. Nvidia's earnings report is anticipated on August 23rd.

title: CoreWeave Secures $2.3 Billion Debt Financing Facility led by Magnetar Capital and Blackstone to Meet Surging Demand and Ongoing Expansion of Specialized Cloud Infrastructure to Power AI
summary: CoreWeave has secured a $2.3 billion debt financing facility led by Magnetar Capital and Blackstone to fuel its expansion of specialized cloud infrastructure for AI. This funding will enable CoreWeave to purchase more compute resources, open new data centers, and grow its staff to meet the surging demand for large-scale GPU-accelerated workloads in the generative AI space. The company plans to have 14 data centers by the end of 2023 and recently unveiled the world's fastest AI supercomputer.

title: Beating the benchmark? How AI-driven ETFs stack up
summary: The article discusses the performance of AI-driven ETFs and whether they offer an information advantage in stock selection compared to traditional benchmarks. It highlights examples like the QRAFT AI-Enhanced U.S. Large Cap Momentum ETF (AMOM) and the AI Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ), noting AMOM's outperformance against a momentum benchmark while AIEQ trails the S&P 500. The piece also explores the potential benefits of AI in portfolio management, such as a lack of emotion and more frequent rebalancing.

title: U.S. chipmaker AMD to invest $400 million in India by 2028
summary: U.S. chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) announced a significant investment of $400 million in India over the next five years, including the establishment of its largest design center in Bengaluru, creating 3,000 new engineering jobs. This move aligns with India's efforts to become a chipmaking hub, attracting other major players like Applied Materials and Micron with its incentive programs. AMD's expansion underscores the country's growing importance in the global semiconductor industry.

title: UMC forecasts utilization rate to fall to 65%
summary: United Microelectronics Corp (UMC) anticipates its factory utilization rate will drop further to about 65% in the current quarter due to prolonged inventory correction and weak end-market demand. This represents the lowest utilization since Q4 2011, and the company finds it difficult to predict a bottom given customer inventory destocking through next quarter. Despite this, UMC plans to expand its 28-nanometer capacity and is doubling its silicon interposer wafer capacity to meet growing demand for AI chips.

title: One in ten retail investors using Chat GPT-style AI to help pick and manage investments
summary: A study by eToro reveals that 11% of retail investors are currently using AI tools like ChatGPT for investment decisions, with this figure rising to 19% among 34-44-year-olds. An additional 35% are open to using AI, citing benefits like time savings and improved decision-making, while 40% remain against it. The findings also indicate strong retail investor confidence in the technology sector, with 30% planning to increase investment in tech for the rest of 2023, specifically highlighting AI.

title: ServiceNow CEO Bill McDermott: Generative AI Could Boost Global GDP By Almost $7 Trillion
summary: ServiceNow CEO Bill McDermott believes generative AI could boost global GDP by nearly $7 trillion, seeing it as a transformative moment comparable to the internet or iPhone. ServiceNow is integrating generative AI into all its workflow offerings and is partnering with Nvidia to accelerate customer value realization from AI. The company also reported strong second-quarter results, exceeding analyst expectations, driven by its role in digital transformation.

title: Micron Delivers Industry's Fastest, Highest-Capacity HBM to Advance Generative AI Innovation
summary: Micron Technology announced it has begun sampling the industry's first 8-high 24 GB HBM3 Gen2 memory, boasting bandwidth greater than 1.2 TB/s and pin speed over 9.2 Gb/s, a significant improvement over existing HBM3 solutions. This new memory offers a 2.5 times performance per watt improvement, setting new benchmarks for AI data center metrics and reducing training times for large language models like GPT-4. Micron's 12-high stack with 36 GB capacity is expected to sample in early 2024, further enhancing capacity and efficiency for generative AI and HPC applications.

title: KT invests over $11 mn in AI software company Moreh
summary: South Korea's KT Corp. is investing 15 billion won ($11.6 million) in Moreh, an AI infrastructure software company, marking its second investment since 2021. This strategic move aims to challenge Nvidia's dominance in AI services and strengthen KT's position as a full-stack AI operator, providing both hardware and software solutions. The investment supports KT's development of hyperscale AI Mi:dm and expansion of B2B AI services, reducing reliance on foreign GPU technologies.

title: Nvidia is ‘dominating’ and could unlock $300 billion in AI revenue by 2027, analyst says
summary: Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh is increasingly optimistic about Nvidia's prospects, projecting the company could tap into $300 billion in AI-related revenue by 2027. Rakesh believes Nvidia will maintain a significant share in the AI server market despite potential future competition. This outlook comes as Nvidia's stock has already seen a 200% increase this year.

title: Microsoft and Meta expand their AI partnership with Llama 2 on Azure and Windows
summary: Microsoft and Meta are expanding their AI partnership, bringing Meta's Llama 2 large language models to Azure and Windows. This collaboration aims to democratize AI by providing developers with open models, enabling them to build generative AI tools and experiences. Azure customers can now fine-tune and deploy Llama 2 models, while Windows developers can run Llama locally, integrating AI safety features from both companies.

title: Fortinet’s stock nabs record closing high, while Microsoft, Nvidia, Broadcom bids all fall short
summary: On Friday, July 14, 2023, several AI-related stocks, including Microsoft, Nvidia, and Broadcom, aimed for record closing highs, but only Fortinet succeeded. Nvidia and Broadcom shares initially rose following positive analyst feedback on their AI chip market potential but ultimately closed down. This illustrates the fluctuating nature of the tech rally driven by artificial intelligence.

title: Aehr Reports Record Revenue and Profit for Fiscal 2023 and Guides for Over 50% Increase in Revenue for Fiscal 2024 on Strength from Semiconductor Wafer Level Test and Burn-in Demand
summary: Aehr Test Systems announced record financial results for fiscal 2023, with net sales reaching $65.0 million and GAAP net income of $14.6 million, driven by demand for semiconductor wafer level test and burn-in products. The company also provided strong guidance for fiscal 2024, projecting revenue of at least $100 million, a 50% increase, and GAAP net income of at least $28 million, reflecting over 90% growth. This growth is attributed to increased adoption of their FOX systems and WaferPak Contactors for silicon carbide in electric vehicles, as well as new opportunities in silicon photonics and gallium nitride markets.

title: HIVE Rebrands, Announces Expansion Into Cloud Computing Services
summary: HIVE Digital Technologies Ltd., formerly HIVE Blockchain, has rebranded and announced its expansion into cloud computing services, utilizing its 38,000 Nvidia GPUs. The company plans to launch "HIVE Cloud" to offer rental services for GPU server clusters, aiming to tap into the high demand for AI-driven computational power. While expanding into a potentially high-margin business, HIVE will also continue its existing bitcoin mining operations.

title: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. – More market share gains expected
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is expected to gain further market share in the data center CPU market and capitalize on opportunities to expand its presence in the data center GPU market due to increased generative AI adoption. The company's margins are projected to grow post-acquisition of Xilinx and Pensando, driven by increasing revenue contributions from its Data Centre and Embedded segments. Phillip Securities Research initiates coverage with an Accumulate recommendation and a target price of US$125.00, anticipating marginal revenue growth in FY23e and re-acceleration in FY24e.

title: Growth-Stock Funds Fly High but Fall Short in 2023′s First Half
summary: Growth-stock funds experienced a strong rebound in the first half of 2023 after significant losses in 2022, with large-growth funds doubling small-growth funds' gains. However, two-thirds of U.S.-centric active managers underperformed stylistically relevant indexes and passive rivals due to untimely sector allocations and light stakes in mega-cap stocks that drove market performance. International and emerging markets showed more modest gains, with some regions outperforming others, leading to a mixed bag for global stocks.

title: Apple makes history as first $3 trillion company amid tech stock surge
summary: Apple Inc. achieved a historic milestone, becoming the first company to reach a $3 trillion market value, driven by investor optimism about its expansion into new markets and a projected easing of interest rate hikes. This accomplishment is set against a backdrop of a broader tech stock surge, with other companies like Tesla and Nvidia also seeing significant gains due to advancements in AI and strategic partnerships. The article highlights Apple's strong financial performance and its reputation as a safe investment, alongside the success of other tech giants.

title: Q3 Stock Market Outlook: Time to Batten Down the Hatches or Raise the Sail?
summary: Morningstar's Q3 2023 stock market outlook suggests that while the U.S. market is still undervalued, the margin of safety has decreased, and the rally in the first half of the year has been disproportionately driven by a few "Magnificent Seven" stocks. Investors are advised to take profits from overextended growth and technology stocks and reallocate to undervalued sectors like communications and real estate, and to value, mid-cap, and small-cap stocks. The outlook anticipates slower market gains due to economic slowdown, tight monetary policy, and reduced credit availability, but expects any future pullbacks to be relatively shallow.

title: XPeng Announces G6 Ultra Smart Coupe SUV
summary: XPeng Inc. has launched its G6 Ultra Smart Coupe SUV in China, built on the SEPA2.0 architecture and priced from 209,900 RMB to 276,900 RMB, with deliveries starting in July 2023. This vehicle features advanced ADAS (XNGP), an 800V powertrain (XPower), integrated aluminum die-casting, and CIB battery-body integration. The G6 boasts a 755 km range, fast-charging capabilities, and a sophisticated design, aiming to solidify XPeng's leadership in the smart EV market.

title: Apple’s market value ends above $3 trillion for the first time
summary: Apple Inc.'s market value surpassed $3 trillion for the first time at the close of a trading session, driven by positive inflation data and confidence in its market expansion strategies. This milestone reflects a 49 percent gain in Apple shares for 2023, amid a tech stock rebound fueled by expectations of slower interest rate hikes from the US Federal Reserve and buzz around artificial intelligence. The company's financial resilience, strong balance sheet, and a recent augmented-reality headset launch contribute to its success, making it one of only five US companies with a valuation exceeding $1 trillion.

title: The Best QQQ Stocks To Buy Now
summary: The article identifies nine top-performing tech and tech-adjacent stocks within the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF, highlighting their growth, innovation, and involvement in artificial intelligence. It details each company's industry, market value, and key factors contributing to its strong performance and future potential, especially in the context of AI advancements. The QQQ ETF itself is noted for its strong returns compared to the S&P 500 over various timeframes.

title: Chipmaker Micron beats on demand from booming AI, easing glut
summary: Micron Technology exceeded third-quarter revenue estimates driven by high demand for its memory chips in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence sector and an easing supply glut in traditional markets. The company's shares rose over 2% after reporting stronger-than-expected earnings and anticipating improved pricing trends. Despite ongoing U.S.-China tech tensions impacting its presence in the Chinese market, Micron expressed confidence in the memory industry's recovery.

title: Nvidia stock falls after CFO says no material impact from prospective wider ban on AI chip sales to China
summary: Nvidia's stock dropped after its CFO, Collette Kress, stated that an expanded U.S. ban on AI chip sales to China would likely have no immediate material impact on the company. However, Kress expressed concern about the long-term effects, suggesting it could lead to a "permanent loss of opportunities" globally. This statement followed reports that the Biden administration was considering widening export bans on AI technology to China.

title: Nvidia and AMD shares fall on report of new U.S. ban on AI chip exports to China
summary: Shares of Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. dropped following a report that the Biden administration is considering a new ban on sales of AI chips to China. This potential ban comes despite Nvidia managing to avoid $400 million in lost sales last year after a previous ban on some chip sales to China. The news impacted both companies with Nvidia shares falling 3% after hours and AMD shares also decreasing by 3%.

title: Active Growth ETF TGRW Doubling Returns of SPY
summary: The T. Rowe Price Growth Stock ETF (TGRW) has demonstrated strong performance in the first half of 2023, doubling the year-to-date returns of the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) with 32.1% compared to SPY's 15.8%. TGRW, which focuses on firms with strong cash flow and above-average earnings growth, is approaching its three-year anniversary and has seen substantial AUM growth. This active growth ETF is outperforming its benchmark thanks to its investment strategy and a competitive expense ratio of 52 basis points.

title: KT to invest $5.4 bn by 2027 to develop AI platforms
summary: South Korea’s telecom service provider KT Corp. plans to invest 7 trillion won ($5.4 billion) by 2027 to become the country’s leading AI service provider, focusing on the robot, healthcare, and education markets. The investment will be allocated to securing super AI source technologies, upgrading related infrastructure, and developing AI service models. KT aims to generate 1.3 trillion won ($1 billion) in revenue from five AI-related service areas by 2025: contact centers, logistics, robots, healthcare, and education.

summary: This article provides a review and aggregate rating for the Fidelity Disruptive Technology ETF (FDTX). MarketBeat calculates this rating by considering the weighted sentiment of analyst ratings for the ETF's constituent stocks. FDTX currently holds a "Moderate Buy" aggregate rating with an average predicted price target reflecting its current share price, based on analyst coverage of 22 companies.

summary: This article provides an aggregate rating and price target for the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) based on Wall Street analyst ratings of its holdings. METV has an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy" and a price target of $16.79, derived from 595 analyst ratings covering 18 companies within its portfolio. The top holdings include tech giants like Apple, Roblox, NVIDIA, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms, along with their individual analyst ratings and potential upsides.

title: The A.I. Race Is Now Between Two Chip Giants Led by Taiwanese American CEOs
summary: The generative A.I. boom has intensified competition between semiconductor giants Nvidia and AMD, who are racing to produce advanced A.I. chips. AMD recently announced the MI300X, a direct competitor to Nvidia's H100, aiming to challenge Nvidia's dominant market share in the A.I. chip sector. Both companies are led by Taiwanese American CEOs, Jensen Huang of Nvidia and Lisa Su of AMD, who share similar backgrounds and have played pivotal roles in their companies' success in the semiconductor industry.

title: AMD is chasing down Nvidia in AI, but one analyst worries the company is ‘somewhat late’
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) is pursuing the lucrative AI data-center market, estimated to be worth $150 billion, following recent product announcements. While many analysts praised AMD's efforts, Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon expressed concerns that AMD is "somewhat late" to the AI race compared to rival Nvidia Corp. Rasgon noted that AMD's AI discussion offered limited "hard numbers" and a timeline that seemed delayed relative to the competition.

title: AMD launches new Instinct MI300X AI chip to take on Nvidia’s GPUs
summary: AMD has launched its new Instinct MI300X AI accelerator chip, designed to compete with Nvidia's GPUs in the generative AI market. The company also introduced its Infinity Architecture Platform, powered by eight MI300X chips, and its ROCm software ecosystem. Despite these announcements, AMD's stock fell due to a lack of major customer endorsements for the new chips and details on pricing.

title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison confirms new gen AI service with Cohere during earnings call
summary: Oracle is partnering with Cohere to launch a new generative AI cloud service that will allow enterprises to train customized large language models (LLMs) using their private data while ensuring privacy and security. Oracle founder Larry Ellison announced the collaboration during the company's Q4 earnings call, highlighting Oracle's existing role in AI development and its significant investment in Cohere. This initiative expands Oracle's offerings in the rapidly growing generative AI market, where it competes with other major cloud providers.

title: ETFs Head-to-Head: BetaShares RBTZ' vs Global X ROBO'
summary: This article compares two ASX-listed ETFs focused on AI and robotics: BetaShares Global Robotics and Artificial Intelligence ETF (ASX: RBTZ) and Global X ROBO Global Robotics & Automation ETF (ASX: ROBO). It analyzes their fund objectives, profiles, holdings, performance, and fees, highlighting ROBO's greater diversification and historical outperformance despite higher management costs. The article concludes that while both offer exposure to AI and robotics, ROBO is larger and more diversified.

title: AMD launches new data-center AI chips, software to go up against Nvidia and Intel
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) unveiled new data-center AI chips and software, including the Instinct MI300X accelerator and MI300A, to compete with Nvidia Corp. and Intel Corp. Despite these announcements at its Data Center & AI Technology Premiere event, AMD's stock declined, finishing down 3.6%. The new products are specifically aimed at handling generative-AI workloads.

title: Insight 2023: NetApp Enhanced Data Pipeline for Hybrid Multi-Cloud AI and Advancements on Secure Storage Vs. Ransomware
summary: NetApp announced significant portfolio updates at Insight 2023, focusing on enhancements to its data pipeline for hybrid multi-cloud AI and advancements in secure storage against ransomware. The company is simplifying AI data pipeline deployment across hybrid multi-cloud environments, while also strengthening data protection with features like autonomous ransomware detection and an extended Ransomware Recovery Guarantee. These innovations aim to address the dual challenges of leveraging AI opportunities and mitigating ransomware threats for customers.

title: Google, Nvidia Back AI Startup That Helps Combat Chip Shortage
summary: CentML, an AI startup focused on improving the efficiency of machine learning systems, has raised $27 million in a seed funding round. The investment, backed by Google's Gradient Ventures, Nvidia Corp., Radical Ventures, Deloitte Ventures, and Thomson Reuters Ventures, aims to help developers optimize computing power for AI training, which could alleviate chip shortages.

title: The Cheap Trick Alphabet Is Using To Boost Its Share Price
summary: Alphabet's 20-for-1 stock split, following similar moves by Apple and Tesla, is unlikely to fundamentally change the company's valuation but aims to make shares more accessible to smaller investors and potentially gain entry into the Dow Jones Industrial Average. While some tech giants saw significant share price boosts post-split, Alphabet's future success might be tempered by changing market conditions. The article suggests Amazon could be the next tech giant to undertake a similar split to boost its stock.

title: 5 Best Momentum ETFs To Buy
summary: This article discusses momentum investing and lists five top momentum ETFs to consider buying, including the JPMorgan U.S. Momentum Factor ETF (JMOM). It highlights JMOM's structure, holdings, and performance, featuring NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) as a key holding. The article also touches on analyst insights and hedge fund sentiment regarding NVIDIA.

title: POET Enters Optical Module Market with 800G Transceiver for Artificial Intelligence Networks
summary: POET Technologies Inc. announced its entry into the optical module market with the Wavelight™, an 800G pluggable transceiver designed for artificial intelligence and cloud data centers. This marks a significant commercial milestone for the company, showcasing its POET Optical Interposer™ technology. The Wavelight modules will be debuted at OFC 2024, with customer sampling beginning in Q3 2024, targeting a rapidly growing market for high-speed transceivers.

title: FTEC: Concentration Increases Volatility (NYSEARCA:FTEC)
summary: The Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF (FTEC) offers strong tech exposure, performing similarly to VGT. However, 45% of its assets are concentrated in Microsoft, Apple, and NVIDIA, which could lead to increased volatility despite a projected 7% upside by year-end 2024. The author, Ricardo Fernandez, highlights the importance of an investor's goals and definition of "tech" when choosing an ETF.

title: What’s Inside Direxion’s Daily Semiconductor Bull and Bear 3x shares?
summary: This article describes the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull (SOXL) and Bear 3X Shares (SOXS) ETFs. title: 3 ETFs That Could Turn Your Portfolio Into a Tech Powerhouse
summary: This article recommends three ETFs to create a diversified tech portfolio, moving beyond reliance on "Magnificent 7" mega-caps. title: Lenovo Vehicle Computing, WeRide Forge Partnership For Autonomous Driving Solutions
summary: Lenovo Vehicle Computing and WeRide have partnered to develop Level 4 autonomous driving solutions for commercial applications. The collaboration will leverage Lenovo's AD1 domain controller, based on the NVIDIA DRIVE Thor platform, and integrate it into WeRide One, a versatile autonomous driving solution. This partnership aims to deliver enhanced autonomous driving products and services globally, focusing on safe and reliable commercial autonomous vehicles.

title: SAP and NVIDIA to Accelerate Generative AI Adoption Across Enterprise Applications Powering Global Industries
summary: SAP and NVIDIA have expanded their partnership to accelerate the adoption of generative AI across SAP's cloud solutions and applications. This collaboration aims to integrate business-specific generative AI capabilities into SAP's Joule copilot and other cloud offerings, leveraging NVIDIA's generative AI foundry services and NIM microservices to fine-tune large language models (LLMs) and enhance data insights. The new integrated capabilities are expected to be available by the end of 2024, enabling customers to automate tasks, improve human resources, and optimize business processes using AI.

title: NVIDIA’s AI models to be deployed on NXP’s edge processing devices portfolio
summary: NXP Semiconductors has announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to enable the deployment of NVIDIA's trained AI models on NXP's edge processing devices through the eIQ machine learning development environment. This integration simplifies the training and deployment of AI models for developers by incorporating the NVIDIA TAO Toolkit into NXP's eIQ environment. The partnership aims to accelerate AI development for industrial and IoT edge applications, providing customers with pre-tested AI models and faster market entry.

title: ServiceNow Washington, DC Release Goes Deep On AI, GenAI
summary: ServiceNow has released its Now Platform Washington, D.C. update, heavily featuring AI and generative AI to boost intelligent automation and simplify workflows. The release introduces Workflow Studio for simplified automation and enhanced Platform Analytics for better performance tracking. It also includes new Sales and Order Management and Security Posture Control tools, all underpinned by advanced GenAI integrations.

title: ServiceNow injects more generative AI capabilities into its workflow platform
summary: ServiceNow announced its new Washington D.C. release, integrating enhanced generative AI capabilities across its workflow platform. Key improvements include Now Assist for IT Operations Management AIOps for quicker issue resolution, and updates to the Virtual Agent feature with dynamic translation. The company also introduced Impact AI Accelerators and partnered with Nvidia to simplify and accelerate AI deployment.

title: Cadence launches data center digital twin offering
summary: Cadence Design Systems has introduced a new AI-driven digital twin platform designed to enhance data center energy efficiency by up to 30%. The "Cadence Reality Digital Twin Platform" virtualizes entire data centers, using AI and physics-based simulations to optimize design and operations for sustainability. Nvidia has integrated this platform with its Omniverse rendering technology and used it to plan its own GB200 cluster deployment.

title: NVIDIA, Huang Win Top Honors in Innovation, Engineering
summary: NVIDIA has been named the world's most innovative company by Fast Company magazine, recognizing its transformative work in putting AI to use across various industries. This accolade follows NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang's induction into the U.S. National Academy of Engineering for his contributions to high-powered graphics processing units and fueling the AI revolution. Leaders from Microsoft, Stanford University, and TSMC have praised Huang's visionary leadership and enduring impact on computing and AI.

title: ServiceNow Named a Leader in Customer Service Solutions by Independent Research Firm
summary: ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) has been named a Leader in the Forrester Wave™: Customer Service Solutions, Q1 2024 for its Customer Service Management (CSM) solution. The recognition highlights ServiceNow's unique focus on "resolution-centric customer service" and its vision to improve customer experience and costs through intelligent self-service and assisted service solutions. The company's AI-powered platform with a single data model is noted for enabling seamless orchestration of customer workflows across various departments.

title: Blackwell: Nvidia's GPU architecture to power new generation of trillion-parameter generative AI models
summary: Nvidia has unveiled its new Blackwell GPU architecture, designed to power trillion-parameter generative AI models with significantly reduced cost and power consumption compared to previous generations. This architecture introduces six transformative technologies, including a custom manufacturing process and enhanced networking capabilities, promising breakthroughs across various advanced computing domains. Blackwell will be available through cloud providers and third-party server manufacturers, enabling a new era of large-scale AI deployment.

title: NVIDIA Launches Blackwell-Powered DGX SuperPOD for Generative AI Supercomputing at Trillion-Parameter Scale
summary: NVIDIA has announced its next-generation AI supercomputer, the NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD, powered by GB200 Grace Blackwell Superchips. This new system is designed for processing trillion-parameter models with constant uptime for generative AI training and inference, featuring liquid cooling, 11.5 exaflops of AI supercomputing, and up to 576 Blackwell GPUs. Additionally, NVIDIA unveiled the DGX B200 system, an air-cooled platform for AI model training, fine-tuning, and inference, providing 15x faster real-time inference for trillion-parameter models.

title: Nvidia and Johnson & Johnson to develop new AI applications for surgery
summary: Johnson & Johnson MedTech is collaborating with Nvidia to develop and scale new artificial intelligence applications for surgery. This partnership aims to integrate AI from pre-op to post-op, helping surgeons by analyzing surgical video, automating documentation, and providing decision support. The technology is expected to improve surgeon training, efficiency, and ultimately, patient outcomes, with initial applications focusing on non-diagnostic tasks like paperwork automation.

title: Johnson & Johnson MedTech partners with Nvidia on AI in surgery
summary: Johnson & Johnson MedTech and Nvidia are partnering to accelerate AI in surgery, aiming to enhance real-time analysis, surgical decision-making, education, and collaboration in the operating room. This collaboration will leverage Nvidia's AI platform for healthcare and J&J MedTech's surgical technologies, focusing on advanced edge computing to process data locally and securely. The goal is to deploy AI-powered solutions more rapidly and scalably within J&J MedTech's digital surgery ecosystem to advance patient care.

title: Johnson & Johnson MedTech Works With NVIDIA to Broaden AI’s Reach in Surgery
summary: Johnson & Johnson MedTech is collaborating with NVIDIA to integrate advanced AI capabilities into its digital ecosystem for surgery. This partnership aims to enhance operating room efficiency and clinical decision-making by leveraging NVIDIA's IGX edge computing platform and Holoscan edge AI platform. The initiative seeks to promote open innovation and provide medical professionals with real-time insights before, during, and after surgical procedures.

title: TSMC and Synopsys Bring Breakthrough NVIDIA Computational Lithography Platform to Production
summary: NVIDIA announced that TSMC and Synopsys are using NVIDIA's cuLitho computational lithography platform in production to accelerate semiconductor manufacturing and enable new generative AI algorithms. This collaboration significantly speeds up compute-intensive lithography workloads, reducing production time and costs while pushing the boundaries for advanced chip scaling, including support for NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture. The integration of cuLitho and new generative AI algorithms enhances efficiency and precision in chip fabrication, addressing bottlenecks in the development of next-generation technologies.

title: NVIDIA Blackwell Platform Arrives to Power a New Era of Computing
summary: NVIDIA has announced the Blackwell platform, a new GPU architecture designed to power the next generation of AI and accelerated computing. The Blackwell platform promises to enable real-time generative AI on trillion-parameter models with significantly reduced cost and energy consumption compared to its predecessor. Major cloud providers and AI companies, including Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, Tesla, and xAI, are expected to adopt Blackwell.

summary: NVIDIA has announced Project GR00T, a general-purpose foundation model for humanoid robots, along with significant updates to its Isaac robotics platform. This initiative includes a new Jetson Thor computer designed for humanoid robots and enhancements to the Isaac platform with generative AI foundation models and simulation tools. Robots powered by GR00T will be capable of understanding natural language and learning skills by observing human actions, marking a major step towards artificial general robotics.

The partnership expands on earlier efforts to bring AI into smart meters and addresses the need to replace aging meters across the U.S.

title: NVIDIA Corp (NVDA) DCF Valuation: Is The Stock Undervalued?
summary: This article analyzes NVIDIA Corp (NVDA) using a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation model. Based on the model's inputs and calculations, including forecasted free cash flows, a 12% discount rate, and a 2% terminal growth rate, NVDA is found to be significantly overvalued. The calculated DCF value of $104.71 per share is substantially lower than its current market price of $925.99, indicating a negative margin of safety.

title: NetApp Turbocharges AI Innovation with Intelligent Data Infrastructure
summary: NetApp announced new capabilities for its intelligent data infrastructure, integrating with NVIDIA's high-performance compute, networking, and software, to maximize the potential of generative AI (Gen AI) projects. summary: SK Hynix is exploring a collaboration with Kioxia Holdings Corp. to produce high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, with a proposal for joint production at existing Kioxia-Western Digital plants in Japan. This move comes as SK Hynix reportedly opposes a merger between Kioxia and Western Digital, fearing it would create the world's largest NAND memory manufacturer. The collaboration would leverage SK Hynix's HBM expertise and Kioxia's facilities to meet soaring demand for AI applications while potentially influencing the Kioxia-Western Digital merger discussions.

The FOX-XP system, capable of testing up to 8,192 high-power optical devices in parallel across nine wafers, expands Aehr's market opportunities in optical I/O and co-packaged optics for data centers and telecommunications.

Its 24Gbyte 8-high HBM3E components will be featured in Nvidia's H200 tensor core GPUs shipping in Q2 2024, potentially positioning Micron ahead of rival SK Hynix in HBM3E production. The company is also preparing a 12-high 36Gbyte HBM3E component for introduction in March 2024, with its stock opening almost 5 percent higher on the news.

summary: ServiceNow and NVIDIA have expanded their partnership to introduce telco-specific generative AI solutions aimed at improving service experiences. The first solution, Now Assist for Telecommunications Service Management (TSM), built on the Now Platform and leveraging NVIDIA AI, is designed to boost agent productivity, speed resolution times, and enhance customer experiences for telecommunications service providers. title: Super Micro Computer shares surge 12% after company files delayed financials by deadline
summary: Super Micro Computer shares surged 12.2% after the AI server company filed its delayed financial results by the Nasdaq's deadline, regaining compliance with filing requirements. The company reported more than doubled sales to $14.99 billion and a net income of $1.15 billion for the fiscal year, despite identifying material weaknesses in internal controls. Super Micro plans to hire more accounting and audit employees and upgrade IT systems to address these issues.

summary: Nvidia reported strong fiscal fourth-quarter earnings, beating Wall Street expectations, with revenue up 78% year-over-year due to high demand for its AI-accelerating GPUs. The company also issued robust guidance for the first quarter, projecting $43 billion in revenue, driven by the anticipated "significant ramp" of its next-generation Blackwell AI chips. While growth rates are moderating as Nvidia scales, its data center business, now 91% of total sales, continues to surge, with CEO Jensen Huang noting "amazing" demand for Blackwell.

title: ZoomInfo CEO says he is buying more stock as shares explode more than 20% higher
summary: ZoomInfo's CEO, Henry Schuck, is buying more company stock after an earnings report caused shares to surge over 20%. Schuck believes the stock is undervalued and plans to continue aggressive share repurchases, with ZoomInfo having already repurchased 12% of outstanding shares last year. The company is investing in AI, notably with its new CoPilot tool, and sees positive traction in customer spending despite cautious 2025 guidance.

title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2025
summary: NVIDIA reported record financial results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year 2025, driven by strong demand for its Data Center products, particularly for Blackwell AI supercomputers. The company announced record quarterly revenue of $39.3 billion and full-year revenue of $130.5 billion, with significant growth in Data Center revenue. NVIDIA also provided an optimistic outlook for the first quarter of fiscal 2026, highlighting continued advancements and partnerships across various sectors including AI, Gaming, Professional Visualization, Automotive, and Robotics.

title: Super Micro files financials just ahead of Nasdaq deadline and says it's 'regained compliance,' stock pops 22%
summary: Super Micro Computer successfully filed its delayed financial results just before the Nasdaq deadline, leading to a 22% surge in its stock during extended trading. The company announced it has regained compliance with Nasdaq's filing requirements after resolving issues stemming from its previous auditor's resignation and internal control weaknesses. Super Micro addressed these internal control issues and confirmed its fiscal 2024 sales more than doubled to $14.99 billion, primarily due to high demand for AI-related components.

title: EXL Reports 2024 Fourth Quarter and Year-End Results; Issues 2025 Guidance
summary: EXL (EXLS) announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full year 2024, reporting significant revenue and earnings growth.
